title: Horizon: Tactile GPU Pool Dashboard & Burst Controls
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a next-generation GPU pool dashboard and control surface focused on rapid operator decisions during bursts and degraded capacity. The Horizon concept emphasizes tactile, glanceable signals (heat-strip, load-spark, and a predictive burst slider) plus an interactable 'burst composer' that lets operators assemble short burst policies with one-handed flows. Goal: reduce mean time to safe-scale (MTTSS) and surface cost-SLA tradeoffs so SREs and platform engineers can react under pressure without context switching to CLI or separate runbooks.
comments: 2025-10-30 - Maya Chen: Initial exploratory sketch uploaded. Focus areas called out: immediate failure modes, cost overlay, and single-action burst commits.

2025-11-02 - Ravi Patel: Implementability check with backend done. Need telemetry endpoints for per-pool predictive load and historical microburst series (1s resolution). Backend owner: ENG-22745 assigned to add endpoints.

2025-11-04 - Elena Ortiz (PM): Requested a lowest-friction fallback: a single confirm CTA for 'emergency burst' that does not require policy authoring. Also asked for audit logging hook for Private deployments.
2025-11-06 - Ravi Patel: Wireframes updated to include cost-SLA overlay. Prototype now simulates cost delta when burst is enabled; requires cost estimator API from Optimize team.

2025-11-09 - Design Review w/ Andreas (Head of Console): Iterate on affordances — replace abstract knobs with a 'drag-to-burst' timeline and a compact quick-apply preset tray. Andreas requests accessibility contrast adjustments.
2025-11-12 - Usability session summary: 6/8 participants completed emergency burst flow in under 14s. Confusion noted around predictive cooldown hints; added tooltip and inline runbook snippet.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity prototype validates single-operator emergency burst flow (start, preview cost impact, confirm)
Design includes fallback compact control for mobile and narrow sidebars
Accessibility: WCAG AA contrast and keyboard-only operations for burst composer
Handoff docs list all required telemetry and APIs (predictive load stream, per-node health, cost estimator)
Audit and rollout metadata surfaced for each burst action (who/when/policy)
decisions: Use a combined visual: heat-strip (real-time health) overlaid with a sparse sparkline for microburst frequency
Burst Composer will support three tiers: quick-presets, guided composer, and advanced policy editor (separate flow)
Preview pane will surface cost delta, expected latency change, and rollback inertia estimate before confirm
tradeoffs: Tactile/graphical controls increase front-end complexity and initial load; mitigated by lazy-loading heavy visuals and server-side thumbnails
Showing cost estimates in the UI requires a near-real-time cost estimator; until available use simulated estimates with clear disclaimer
Compact controls reduce feature density; chosen to favor speed over configuring every detailed field inline
user_testing: Participant profile: Platform engineers and SREs from 3 pilot customers
Key finding: Operators wanted a safe preview step more than an undo button; emphasis on clear rollback time
Key finding: Presets are used 4x more often than bespoke composer in first-run sessions
Accessibility note: Keyboard users prefer explicit 'Apply' button rather than drag gestures; ensure parity
